overview: Both sides fianchetto their king's bishop and delay central commitment. White usually continues Bg2, then c4, d4 or Nf3 and d3, and transposes to the King's Indian Attack, English, Réti or a reversed Modern/Pirc structure. The game is a flexible manoeuvring fight with few forcing lines, and a draw is the most common result.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto with Bg2, then c4 and Nc3 or d4 for a flexible centre
Build a King's Indian Attack with Nf3, d3, O-O and e4
Keep options open and transpose to the Catalan or English

black_ideas.idea: Mirror with ...Bg7 and ...Nf6, castle and play ...d6 and ...e5
Take the centre with ...d5 or ...e5 once the bishops are placed
Equalise by symmetry and look for counterplay on the long diagonal

typical_structures.structure: Mirror fianchetto structure, with d3 or d4 against ...d6 or ...d5
Reversed Modern or Pirc set-ups depending on whether White plays e4

character.notes: Quiet and low-risk for both sides; the position is not forcing and hard to attack.

structure.notes: Centre not committed: flank openings with undecided pawns, flexible.

approach.notes: A fianchetto set-up White uses against almost anything and which transposes to KIA, Réti or English; plans matter more than move order.

level.notes: Clear plans, little to memorise, but the transpositions and manoeuvring need judgement.

sublines_that_differ.name: Benko Opening with 2.Bg2 Bg7 3.c4
sublines_that_differ.how: Becomes a reversed English with a symmetrical fianchetto structure.
